newsitem.title: USA: No Ramsey family representative to view DNA test.
newsitem.headline: No Ramsey family representative to view DNA test.

text.p: Attorneys for the parents of slain six-year-old beauty pageant winner JonBenet Ramsey have decided not to have a representative present when DNA tests are conducted on evidence, the family said on Friday.
A brief statement issued by Ramsey family spokesman Pat Korten said the family's lawyers had determined that it was "unnecessary" to have an observer present.
Officials said Thursday the DNA testing at the Cellmark Diagnostics Laboratory in Maryland had not begun because the Ramsey family had not yet accepted an offer to have a representative present.
The DNA testing will take about six weeks.
Officials said last week that a family representative would be allowed to view the testing, but did not say why. They described the offer as a "conservative" approach by the district attorney.
Suspects charged with a crime in Colorado are allowed to view DNA testing because a sample could be destroyed, making further testing impossible.
The girl's body was found Dec. 26 in a basement in the family's home in Boulder by her father, John Ramsey, some eight hours after her mother said she found a ransom note demanding $118,000.
No arrests have been made and no suspects have been named in the 13-week-old murder investigation.
